T-004.Title: Wave 2 — disable revokes the secret and gates every incoming route

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: mt_ext_disable calls auth::revoke_secret for the extension (besides registry.disable) and enforces the revocation CONTRACT, not just the call: revoke_secret becomes Result-honest — a keychain delete_credential error propagates (today it is logged as BLOCK_REVOKE_FAILED and swallowed, auth.rs:127-134, while get_secret reads the keychain FIRST, auth.rs:93-97, so a failed delete keeps the old token authenticating behind an apparently successful disable; only a confirmed NoEntry may count as absence. Entry creation, credential-store access, delete, read-back and in-memory store errors must remain distinguishable from confirmed absence) — and disable verifies absence after the revoke: a strict revocation read-back must prove absence from both the persistent store and the memory fallback before disable reports success. The current best-effort get_secret can return None on a backend error and cannot supply that proof. A failed revocation must remain observable as a failure and the disabled extension must stay fenced for that attempt; when the revoke errors or the secret provably survives, mt_ext_disable surfaces the failure instead of claiming success — as a stable short code (ext_disable_revoke_failed) whose free-form detail goes ONLY to the BLOCK_ log marker, mapped by the gallery to ONE new localized key extensions.disableFailed landing in all ten shipped locales (the spec's ten-locale rule for the one refusal notice this wave makes user-visible; static/locales/*.json joins the observed scope and the locale completeness gate stays green) — so previously issued tokens stop authenticating the moment a SUCCESSFUL disable returns; re-enabling does not resurrect the old secret — the extension re-pairs; the shared incoming gate from T-003 is adopted by handle_ext_context and handle_ext_apply for its token-validity and ExtRegistry.enabled steps only — no capability is invented for them (the spec's Goal grants context/apply the enabled check alone; the protocol vocabulary has no context/apply capability today), so an enabled paired extension of ANY declared capability keeps /ext/context and /ext/apply access exactly as today; the text.insert capability enforcement stays exclusive to text-insert (the gate helper takes the required capability as an Option); /stream/* routes keep their session-auth semantics unchanged.

m045_ext/tests.rs proves, every leg NAMED and selected by the task command's grep legs: disable_revokes_and_verifies_absence, disable_surfaces_revoke_failure, disable_refuses_unverified_revocation, enabled_extension_passes_all_three_routes, fresh_pairing_restores_access. After mt_ext_disable the OLD token is refused on /ext/context, /ext/apply and /ext/text-insert (401), and the stored secret is gone — the strict read-back used by disable proves absence, and the ordinary get_secret also yields None; a revoke failure injected through a seam the Result-honest refactor itself introduces — an injectable credential backend for entry creation, delete and strict read-back (a #[cfg(test)]-visible hook or narrow trait, declared new by this plan: auth.rs has NO seam today, round 12 — the MEM_STORE entry is removed unconditionally before keyring is ever touched, and keyring's set_default_credential_builder mock is process-global and NOT the declared seam) — leaves disable reporting failure (the stable code), never a silent success. The unverified-revocation test covers both entry creation failure and read-back access failure after a reported delete, with the memory fallback empty. A confirmed NoEntry is the successful absence case; a fresh pairing after successful disable restores access on all three routes; an enabled extension of ANY declared capability still passes context/apply (the legit-path companion the TokMo EditAgent flows live on — handler-level context/apply tests do not exist today) — the audit's disabled-extension replay scenario is closed end-to-end, including the keychain-first mode the in-memory seam alone never observes.

T-005.Title: Wave 2 — real URL parsing for base_url, final-URL revalidation, no redirects

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: src-tauri/Cargo.toml gains url = "2" as a direct dependency (2.5.8 already in the lockfile transitively — no new vendor code); validate_manifest parses discovery.base_url with Url::parse and validates the PARSED host against the loopback set (typed Url::host() comparison against 127.0.0.1, localhost and ::1, with the string split(':') removed): userinfo of any form is rejected (username/password present → error), non-http(s) schemes rejected as today, and a parsed host that only LOOKS loopback before parsing (http://localhost:1@evil.example/) now fails because the parsed host is evil.example; IPv6 forms validate through the parser's canonical host — the bracketed [::1] is accepted; the BARE ::1 spelling is refused exactly as today (round-13 probe: the current split parser already yields an empty host for it, so the match-arm's bare spelling is dead code — the Url::parse rewrite preserves the refusal rather than tightening it; no honest manifest uses it).

invoke_extension re-validates the FINAL URL (base_url trimmed + invoke_path joined, parsed again) with the same loopback+no-userinfo rule before any request is built, and the reqwest client is built with redirect Policy::none() (the locked reqwest implementation strips Authorization on cross-origin hops but can still follow the redirect and, for body-preserving redirects, replay the extension payload); a redirect response surfaces as an invoke error, never a followed request. The same treatment covers the second outgoing client round 4 found still on the default policy: probe_health (discovery.rs:122 — base_url+health_path joined, reqwest builder without a redirect policy) gets the same final-URL revalidation and the same Policy::none(), so NO reqwest client in m045_ext follows redirects and no probe request can be carried off-loopback by a 30xx (the probe carries no bearer today — the closed leak is telemetry: machine IP and the fact of the extension's presence).

Every promised leg of T-005's test set carries a NAME, and the task command's grep legs select them (round 10 swept the whole set after rounds 8-9 caught unnamed legs one by one): manifest_rejects_userinfo_url (http://localhost:1@evil.example/ rejected at validate_manifest); invoke_rejects_userinfo_final_url (the same URL rejected again at the invoke-side final-URL revalidation); manifest_accepts_loopback_hosts (valid loopback manifests still validate — 127.0.0.1, localhost, and the bracketed [::1], with ports and paths, closing the canonicalization hazard of the current two-spelling match arm and covering hosts the single pre-existing 127.0.0.1 fixture never did; the bare ::1 spelling is refused exactly as today — the current split parser already rejects it, and the match-arm's bare spelling is dead code (round-13 probe)); manifest_rejects_non_loopback_host_without_userinfo (http://evil.example/ rejected by the parsed-host loopback rule itself, with the IPv4-mapped form [::ffff:127.0.0.1] — canonicalized non-loopback per the round-5 probe — rejected too, so a broken loopback comparison cannot hide behind the userinfo rejections; round 8: every earlier manifest negative carried userinfo and died before the host check); invoke_rejects_host_changing_path (exercise both a loopback base with an explicit port and the same base with a path prefix. The absolute-URL suffix can produce a parse error for the port-only base, or remain literal path data on the loopback host when the base has a path. The scheme-relative suffix also remains path data with the current concatenation. Assert that none produces a request to a different recipient, and explicitly assert the resulting host for parseable variants); invoke_redirect_response_not_followed (a redirect-bearing response surfaces as an error, never a followed request — the client builder's policy asserted by test for BOTH clients, invoke and probe_health); invoke_honest_loopback_ok (against a local 127.0.0.1 TcpListener serving a one-shot 200 JSON response — binding loopback only, so the no-network rule of the parser's negative tests is not stretched to external hosts: an honest loopback manifest with a non-redirect response invokes successfully, the payload is received, and the refusal-all-redirects policy never rejects an honest response); probe_health_honest_loopback_ok (the same local-listener pattern: an honest loopback manifest's health probe still returns healthy=true — without it, a revalidation bug rejecting every URL would flip the whole gallery offline while every pinned test stayed green). Both validation sites share one loopback+no-userinfo helper, making the manifest-side negatives cover the invoke side alike.

Rust tests (a #[cfg(test)] seam for the validation logic) carry a pinned link_click_ name prefix — link_click_refuses_bare_command, link_click_refuses_prefixed_command, link_click_opens_document_sibling, link_click_refuses_escape_from_document_dir, link_click_http_unchanged — so the task command and its grep guard select them (cargo exits 0 on a filter matching zero tests; the pinned naming is the anti-vacuity contract, mirroring T-007's ancestor_ discipline). T-007.Title: Wave 3 — check_path resolves the nearest existing ancestor for new paths

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: When the requested target is missing, check_path walks the requested path and its parents by directory entry (nearest_existing_ancestor uses symlink_metadata). Only NotFound advances the walk. A dangling link is an existing entry; canonicalize it and reject if the destination cannot be resolved, before a caller can open or create through that entry. Reject other filesystem errors. Compare the canonical existing entry against the canonical sandbox, preserving the existing permissive-root prefix exemption and Windows prefix handling; canonicalization and sandbox fencing for existing targets are preserved (symlinked existing files still canonicalize and fence as today — the outside-overwrite regression stays covered); the not-exists walk handles a fully non-existing tree by pinning the check to the sandbox when no ancestor exists before the sandbox root, and Windows drive-prefix/UNC behavior (C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE strip_device_prefix semantics) is preserved in the ancestor comparison.

m010/m013b tests prove: a new text file, a new binary write and a create_dir_all through a parent symlink pointing OUTSIDE the sandbox are all rejected (SymlinkEscapesSandbox error, BLOCK_ marker); the same symlink pointing INWARD still works; overwrite of an existing outside file via symlink stays rejected (regression); a plain new path with an existing in-sandbox parent writes as before. A dangling final-component symlink whose missing target has an existing writable parent outside the sandbox is refused before creation; exercise the real text and binary write seams and assert the outside target remains absent. The permissive-root suite stays green. The new tests carry a shared ancestor_ name prefix (ancestor_escape_text_new, ancestor_escape_binary_new, ancestor_escape_mkdir in the m010 seam; ancestor_inward_ok, ancestor_existing_outside_regression and ancestor_dangling_leaf_refused in the m013b/fs seam) — the naming is pinned because cargo exits 0 on a filter matching zero tests, so unnamed filters can pass vacuously. Because every write path (fs_write_inner, binary write, mkdir) funnels through check_path, fixing the helper closes all three audit variants with one change.

The spec's NonGoals hold in the diff: no pairing-UX redesign, no confirm dialog for executable link targets (hard block only), no descriptor-based write rework, no muya sanitizer change, no live-server listener-surface change (still 127.0.0.1, OS-assigned port, MAS no-listener) — verified by the diff touching none of those designs.

Verification.Command: sh -c "npm test && cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --bin mark"

C-1.Situation: The release job's attribution and SBOM steps executed with the npm registry unreachable (offline runner simulation), plus a hostile edit reintroducing npx --yes into release.yml.
C-1.Expected: Both steps run to completion from lockfile-installed binaries (npm ci already installed them; no registry contact); the guard test fails the hostile edit naming file and line; cargo-tool pinning untouched; the README leg shows no unpinned wrangler instruction.

C-2.Situation: A local process POSTs /ext/text-insert with no token, a wrong token, a valid token of a disabled extension, and a valid token of an enabled extension lacking text.insert; then the full authorized path.
C-2.Expected: The first four are refused 401/403 with an AUTH-style BLOCK_ marker and mt::text::op is never emitted; the authorized request inserts text carrying the requester's real extension_id. The Mark body fixture preserves the server schema and the actual supported paired client supplies separate interoperability evidence.

C-3.Situation: An extension is paired, then disabled in the gallery; its held token replays /ext/context, /ext/apply and /ext/text-insert; it re-pairs after re-enabling.
C-3.Expected: Every replay after successful disable is refused and persistent and memory credential absence was verified. An unavailable credential backend fails the disable operation visibly. A fresh pairing after successful disable restores full access; /stream/* session semantics unchanged.

C-4.Situation: A manifest with base_url http://localhost:1@evil.example/ (and IPv6/absolute-invoke_path variants); a loopback manifest answering 302 to an external recipient; an honest loopback manifest.
C-4.Expected: The userinfo manifest fails validation (parsed host is evil.example); the final-URL validation rejects any recipient outside the allowlist and tests the actual parsed host for path-prefixed base URLs; the 302 is never followed (Policy::none(), both outgoing clients) and surfaces as an invoke error; honest loopback manifests (127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1], ports, paths) validate and a non-redirect invoke succeeds exactly as before — proven by the pinned invoke_honest_loopback_ok companion against a local 127.0.0.1 listener (the zero-network rule covers the parser's negative tests; the companion binds loopback only); refusing ALL redirects is the recorded tightening over the spec's different-recipient minimum, and refusing the bare ::1 spelling matches today's behavior (the current parser already rejects it — round-13 probe); the health probe carries the same policy, with no bearer ever attached to a probe request.

C-5.Situation: Ctrl/Cmd+click on a relative link to a sibling .command (and .app); a relative link to a sibling notes.md inside a fenced workspace and outside it; an http(s) link.
C-5.Expected: Executable targets are refused with a log marker before the opener is called (check_shell_open_extension, sandbox-independent); sibling document/image links of ANY document open as today — the document's own directory is the fence, so a document opened outside a fenced workspace (the production state round 8 pinned) keeps opening its siblings; http(s) handling is byte-identical; a relative target escaping the document's directory is refused by check_path.

C-6.Situation: A workspace contains a symlinked folder pointing to a writable location outside the sandbox; a new text file, a new binary/image write and a mkdir are directed through it; the same symlink points inward in a second workspace; an existing outside file is targeted through a symlink; a Windows drive-root sandbox exercises the permissive-root path.
C-6.Expected: All three outward creations are rejected via the nearest-existing-ancestor canonicalization (one check_path change covers fs_write_inner, binary writes and create_dir_all); the inward symlink still works; the existing-file outside-overwrite stays rejected and a dangling final link cannot create its outside target; permissive-root and drive-prefix semantics are preserved.

C-7.Situation: Runtime and CI cost of the wave: URL parse at manifest load and per invoke; registry lookup plus token check on every incoming /ext/* request; ancestor walk on every new-file save; two more devDependencies in npm ci; the release job's SBOM/attribution steps on local binaries.
C-7.Expected: No measurable interactive-path regression: the ancestor walk is a bounded parent walk ending at an existing directory (one canonicalize per save of a new file), the URL parse is microseconds and off the editing path, the registry candidate snapshot is in memory but bearer validation can access the OS keychain. Limit text-insert checks to enabled capability candidates, keep native lookups off the async request executor, and record the lookup count and latency against the current client flow before claiming no regression; release attribution/SBOM steps run the same tools from local binaries with no wall-clock regression; budgets (1800 s combined whole-suite, 600 s filtered) rest on recorded numbers only: the sibling C-RENDER-REVIEW-FIXES plan record (suite 119-306 s), the archived full-suite log t005-npm-test-unit.log (133.72 s), and CI job walls 167-461 s (renderer unit with setup and coverage) — npm ci grows by the two direct devDependencies' transitive closure (~230 packages, one-time install, cache-warm afterwards); plausibility-checked at plan time, re-measured at T-009.

C-8.Situation: Process truth: LINKS headers, graph and verification deltas, serial shared-file arcs, satisfied archival prerequisites, and drift from the recorded imported CI baseline.
C-8.Expected: Six governed headers carry the change reference; the nine M-/V-M- anchors' deltas (including M-001's amended command records) reference C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES and the new tests by name; live_server.rs serialized T-003 ≺ T-004 and tests.rs T-003 ≺ T-004 ≺ T-005; the archived renderer/stats prerequisites are satisfied and current CI-imported graph entries are preserved; the security candidate must retain zero current-state integrity errors. The old nested-worktree/missing-spec errors are absent from the isolated baseline, and the imported CI repair fixes the tree-treefiles map; do not carry them as present product defects. The four existing Python heuristic warnings are not new failures.

Review.Run: dwfrun-21fcf99d-1c21-478b-bd42-82465618bd32, round 2 (the confirmation pass over unchanged artifacts)
Review.Result: 2 blocking findings, both CORR, both mechanical truths of the execution environment.

Applied.Fix: Blocking (CORR-F-1): the T-004 locale loop replaced with a variable-free form — grace executes plan commands via the OUTER $SHELL -lc (grace4/command-runner.ts:465), which expanded $f to an empty string before the inner sh -c ever saw the loop, so grep read redirected stdin, exited 1, and the command failed even with the key present in all ten locales (the reviewer replicated the exact two-layer mechanism); the loop is now "! grep -L disableFailed static/locales/*.json | grep -q ." — grep -L names any file lacking the key, so the leg fails exactly when a locale is missing it and needs no shell variable.

Blocking (CORR-F-2): the generic-refactor boundary extended to the files it actually touches — live_bridge.rs joins the observed scope and T-003 declares its five emit functions generic over R (app: &AppHandle<R>; bare &AppHandle today, called from live_server.rs at :615/:768/:839/:993/:1178), without which the mock-runtime harness does not compile for R = MockRuntime.

Review.Deferred: None — every round-15 blocking finding is addressed above; corner notes live in the gate report card.

Review.Run: Bounded manual four-corner review in Codex, main 296dc5f0, after the owner stopped dwfrun-5badb083. No automated review resumed.
Review.Result: Five material issues confirmed by repository sources, locked dependency source, or a local probe. This pass grants no independent clean verdict.

Applied.Fix: F-006: an exists()-based walk skips a dangling leaf. A Rust probe followed the planned logic, then File::create created its missing target outside a temporary sandbox. An entry-aware walk using symlink_metadata rejected the same case and preserved ordinary in-sandbox creation. T-007 now pins an end-to-end dangling-leaf write test.

F-002: the Mark-shaped request proves Mark's server schema only. TokMo origin/main af97d7f2 sends a cap/payload envelope from IpcSink, and its transport's bearer is optional. No production constructor was found in that revision. T-003 now requires evidence from the supported paired client and records any coordinated rollout dependency without opening an unauthenticated path. Candidate filtering and the keychain cost are recorded.

F-003: treating unavailable storage as absent could let an old keychain token survive an apparently successful disable. auth.rs's get_secret falls back to None on backend errors. T-004 now requires strict absence and an explicit test for entry and read-back failure.
F-004: a token named --no-install after a positional npx argument can be passed to the program. T-001 now uses direct local binaries and forbids npm package executors in the two release source files.

F-005: a base URL with a path can parse an absolute-looking suffix as path data on the same host. The verification now proves recipient containment for both base shapes and uses typed parsed hosts. The redirect rationale reflects reqwest 0.13.5 stripping cross-origin Authorization while still potentially forwarding the payload.

Review.Deferred: Implementation and live client verification remain pending plan approval. The existing release pairing confirmation stays within the approved non-goal. Wave 1 must reconcile the shared release workflow with C-CI-CD-AUDIT-FIXES before editing it.
